title: Molecular biological and immunological determinants of severe RSV infections in children
summary:
The aim of this study is to identify immunological and molecular biological factors that are associated with a severe course of RSV infection in children. RSV (respiratory syncytial virus) can lead to severe respiratory diseases, particularly in infants and young children. The exact causes of this are still largely unknown. In this study, we are investigating how the immune system reacts to the virus, but also which characteristics of the virus are associated with severe cases.
For this purpose, nasal swabs and blood samples from RSV-infected and non-infected children are analyzed. Special methods such as flow cytometry and transcriptome analyses are used to investigate which subpopulations of immune cells are active in the mucous membrane. In addition, the RS viruses are examined genetically and in cell culture experiments in order to identify any genetic characteristics of the virus.
The data obtained will be compared with the course of the children's illnesses in order to determine whether certain immunological or molecular characteristics are associated with severe illnesses. 
Another focus of the study is the possible development of virus variants that could escape the immune system. This is particularly relevant as the monoclonal antibody nirsevimab has been recommended as a preventive measure for all infants since June 2024. The study aims to detect at an early stage whether the virus develops mutations that could reduce the effectiveness of this antibody therapy.
In the long term, this research will help to better understand the mechanisms of severe RSV courses and improve treatment and prevention for affected children.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Study participants are patients of the University Hospital Düsseldorf
- Consent to participate in the study by the parents or legal guardians and consent to participation by the study participant (from pre-school age)
- Symptoms indicative for a respiratory infection and/or PCR or POCT test positive for RSV (target group) or alternatively RSV PCR or POCT test negative for RSV (control group, preferably comparable in terms of age and previous illnesses)
Exclusion criteria:
- No consent to the study
- Age ≥18 years
- Study participation is not reasonable at this time for health reasons
